agree.reason: It directly answers the GM's belief about the renovation with the 7.9-to-8.2 rise that happened before work started, and gives a concrete budget plan, so a GM who already likes the writer could well be moved, though the outside candidate's larger-hotel experience is only partly offset.

honest.reason: It drops the 'main reason' claim, says the renovation clearly helped, and keeps the facts accurate, but 'people I trained' and 'an outside hire would need months' go a little past what the facts show.

works_the_facts.reason: It quotes the raw figures but never works them out: the pre-renovation pace (0.3 in 5 months against 0.4 in the 13 months after), turnover falling from 64% to 36%, and training cut by 44% are all left uncomputed, even though each is the strongest true form of its number.

right_comparison.reason: The renovation is set against the pre-renovation trend and the outside candidate is described fairly, but the before-and-after pace of the score is never laid side by side, so the trend comparison stays loose.

qualification.reason: The commitments have deadlines (finance course in 3 months, wait-time plan in 30 days, weekly controller sessions), but none sets a measurable target or says what happens if it is missed.

objections.reason: It meets the reader's three likely objections (the renovation, the budget and the outside candidate's experience) with facts from the brief, and it raises no objection those facts already answer.

fit.reason: It is a tight one-page memo as asked, but it leaves bracket placeholders for the GM's name and the writer's name even though both were known, while naming Ben Oduya, which is inconsistent.
